findings.description:
ICE PACK TEST

INDICATION: Evaluation of right ptosis.

TECHNIQUE: Crushed ice in a surgical glove applied over the closed right upper eyelid for 2 minutes. Marginal reflex distance 1 (MRD1) measured immediately before and after application.

RESULTS:
  Right MRD1 before application: 2.0 mm.
  Right MRD1 after application (2 minutes): 4.5 mm.
  Improvement: 2.5 mm.

IMPRESSION: Positive ice pack test (improvement in ptosis of at least 2 mm after cooling). Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Positive ice pack test: right MRD1 improved from 2.0 mm to 4.5 mm (2.5 mm) after 2 minutes of cooling

findings.description: Lobulated, circumscribed mass 3.6 x 2.9 x 3.1 cm; T1 intermediate, T2 mildly hyperintense; heterogeneous enhancement; no signal drop on opposed-phase imaging; intact capsule

output.impression: 1. Encapsulated 3.6 cm anterior mediastinal soft-tissue mass without chemical-shift signal drop or invasion, most consistent with a thymoma. 2. No lymphadenopathy.

findings.description:
BEDSIDE RESPIRATORY FUNCTION TESTING

INDICATION: Generalized fatigable weakness with bulbar symptoms; baseline before thymectomy.

MEASUREMENTS (seated; weight 88.1 kg, height 178 cm):
  FVC: 3.60 L (predicted 4.30 L; 84% predicted; 41 mL/kg)
  MIP (NIF): -54 cmH2O (L; lower limit of normal for age and sex about -65 cmH2O)
  MEP: 86 cmH2O (L; lower limit of normal about 100 cmH2O)
  Single-breath count: 30
  Cough: adequate
  No fall in FVC between seated and supine measurement.

IMPRESSION: 1. Mildly reduced inspiratory and expiratory pressures (MIP -54, MEP 86 cmH2O). 2. FVC preserved (84% predicted, 41 mL/kg). Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Mildly reduced MIP (-54 cmH2O) and MEP (86 cmH2O); FVC preserved at 3.60 L (84% predicted, 41 mL/kg)

action_criteria.expected_evidence: AChR binding antibody 6.4 nmol/L (reference <= 0.02) with blocking 55% and modulating 72%; TSH 1.4 and free T4 normal on levothyroxine; anti-TPO 148 IU/mL
action_criteria.label: Order AChR binding antibody and thyroid function with thyroid antibodies
action_criteria.rationale: Fatigable right ptosis, diplopia, chewing and speech fatigue with proximal weakness: AChR binding antibody (RIA or cell-based assay) first, with thyroid function on levothyroxine because thyroid dysfunction coexists with and aggravates MG (Evoli, Neurol Sci 2019; Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: 3 Hz decrement in deltoid 16%, nasalis 19% and masseter 21% with normal baseline CMAPs, no post-exercise facilitation (6%) and normal nerve conductions
action_criteria.label: Order repetitive nerve stimulation at 3 Hz in facial, masticatory and proximal muscles
action_criteria.rationale: Low-rate RNS of the weak facial, masseter and deltoid muscles documents the postsynaptic decrement; brief exercise testing excludes presynaptic facilitation, and the nerve conductions exclude a diabetic neuropathy as a confounder (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025; Evoli, Neurol Sci 2019).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Extensor digitorum communis mean MCD 74 microseconds with increased jitter in 15 of 20 pairs and blocking in 6
action_criteria.label: Single-fibre EMG (not needed once RNS is diagnostic)
action_criteria.rationale: SFEMG is reserved for a normal RNS or seronegative disease; with high AChR titres and a clear decrement it adds nothing to the diagnosis (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right MRD1 improves from 2.0 to 4.5 mm after 2 minutes of ice
action_criteria.label: Bedside ice pack test of the right ptosis
action_criteria.rationale: Fatigable right ptosis in a diabetic man in whom a cranial neuropathy is the anchoring alternative: an MRD1 improvement of at least 2 mm after cooling points to the neuromuscular junction.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Well-circumscribed 3.6 x 2.9 x 3.1 cm anterior mediastinal mass without invasion, most consistent with thymoma
action_criteria.label: Order contrast CT of the mediastinum for thymoma
action_criteria.rationale: Mediastinal imaging is indicated in every patient with MG to detect thymoma (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025); a thymoma is an indication for resection regardless of MG severity (Sanders 2016).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: MIP -54 and MEP 86 cmH2O mildly reduced; FVC 3.60 L (84% predicted, 41 mL/kg); no crisis threshold met
action_criteria.label: Measure FVC, MIP and MEP before surgery
action_criteria.rationale: Bulbar symptoms and a planned thymectomy: FVC in mL/kg, MIP and MEP stage respiratory muscle strength and set the baseline for anaesthesia (20/30/40 rule, Lawn, Arch Neurol 2001).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Beta-blocker caution in MG and additive bradycardia; steroid hyperglycaemia on metformin
action_criteria.label: Check pyridostigmine and prednisone against his metoprolol and metformin
action_criteria.rationale: He takes a beta-blocker, which can worsen MG and adds bradycardia with pyridostigmine, and metformin, whose glycaemic control prednisone will disturb (ruling 6: a concrete interaction that changes monitoring).

prohibited_recommendations: Do not start high-dose prednisone (above 20 mg/day) as an outpatient; start low and titrate, or start high dose only with inpatient monitoring, because initial steroid-induced worsening can precipitate crisis.

Avoid fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides and IV magnesium unless no alternative exists and the patient is monitored; use non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers only at reduced dose with quantitative monitoring.
Do not attribute fatigable ptosis, diplopia or bulbar weakness to a diabetic cranial neuropathy or a functional cause before AChR antibody testing and neurophysiology.
required_recommendations: Refer to thoracic surgery for complete thymectomy with resection of the thymoma: a thymoma is an indication for surgery regardless of MG severity (Sanders 2016)

Optimise MG before surgery because of bulbar weakness and reduced MIP: IVIG 2 g/kg (about 175 g over 2-5 days) or plasma exchange pre-operatively, with the anaesthetist informed (reduced-dose non-depolarising neuromuscular blockade with quantitative monitoring)
Start pyridostigmine 30 mg three times daily and titrate to 60 mg four to five times daily, monitoring resting heart rate because he takes metoprolol

Start prednisone at 10-20 mg/day and increase gradually with monitoring of bulbar and respiratory function for early steroid-induced worsening; add a steroid-sparing agent (azathioprine after TPMT testing) if long-term steroids are needed
Monitor capillary glucose during prednisone and escalate diabetes treatment (for example basal insulin) for steroid-induced hyperglycaemia
Review metoprolol: beta-blockers can worsen MG, so switch to a non-beta-blocker antihypertensive (for example amlodipine or an ACE inhibitor) if weakness worsens or blood pressure needs adjustment
Give him a list of drugs that can worsen MG and check every new prescription against it

avoided_actions.rationale: MG is a disorder of the neuromuscular junction; EEG has no diagnostic role (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).
CSF has no role in MG and nothing in this presentation raises Miller Fisher syndrome or a CNS cause (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).
FDG-PET is not part of the MG or thymoma work-up here; contrast CT (or MRI) of the mediastinum characterises the mass before resection (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).
A brain MRI has already been done (age-appropriate white matter changes only); repeat imaging is reserved for negative serology and neurophysiology or a central mimic (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).
No cardiac symptom or sign, and the CT shows no pericardial involvement; echocardiography adds nothing to the MG work-up.
Regular rhythm at 68/min and no palpitations or syncope; cardiac monitoring is not part of the MG work-up.

accepted: Myasthenia gravis, generalized (MGFA Class IIb), AChR antibody-positive, with thymoma (3.6 cm anterior mediastinal mass)

differential.key_features: Thymic carcinoma is rarely associated with MG; the encapsulated, well-circumscribed mass with preserved fat planes and no lymphadenopathy favours thymoma; histology at resection decides.

A diabetic third nerve palsy is acute, usually painful and does not fluctuate, and a sixth nerve palsy does not cause ptosis; here the right ptosis and abduction deficit fluctuate and fatigue, with bulbar and limb fatigability, a decrement and positive AChR antibodies.
TSH 1.4 and free T4 normal on levothyroxine (anti-TPO positive, consistent with treated Hashimoto thyroiditis); hypothyroid myopathy does not cause fatigable ptosis or an RNS decrement.
Normal baseline CMAPs, a 3 Hz decrement and no post-exercise facilitation (6%), preserved reflexes, prominent ocular signs; AChR binding antibody strongly positive.
Months of fluctuating, fatigable symptoms with bulbar and limb fatigability are not a vascular pattern, and the prior brain MRI showed only age-appropriate white matter changes.

key_clinical_evidence: Fluctuating, fatigable weakness with a diurnal pattern (worse in the evening) is the clinical hallmark of MG; fixed weakness suggests an alternative diagnosis.
Fatigable ptosis with an ocular motor deficit that varies, plus bulbar and limb fatigability, is not explained by a diabetic cranial mononeuropathy.
A high AChR binding titre (6.4 nmol/L) with a 16-21% decrement on 3 Hz RNS establishes generalized AChR-positive MG; SFEMG is not needed.
Mediastinal CT with contrast is indicated in every patient with MG to detect thymoma; here it shows a 3.6 cm encapsulated anterior mediastinal mass most consistent with thymoma.
A thymoma is an indication for thymectomy regardless of MG severity; bulbar weakness and a reduced MIP call for pre-operative IVIG or plasma exchange.
Metoprolol (beta-blocker) can worsen MG and adds bradycardia with pyridostigmine; prednisone will raise glucose in his diabetes.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A diabetic third nerve palsy is acute, usually painful and fixed, and a sixth nerve palsy does not cause ptosis; this right ptosis and abduction deficit fluctuate and fatigue, come with bulbar and limb fatigability, and the case is AChR-antibody positive with a decrement.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute ocular symptoms to diabetic cranial neuropathy.

sequence_constraints.reason: Repetitive nerve stimulation is done first; SFEMG follows when RNS is normal (Jacob 2025).
AChR antibody testing precedes single-fibre EMG; SFEMG is reserved for seronegative patients or a normal RNS (Jacob 2025).

findings.description: Well-circumscribed, lobulated, encapsulated-appearing anterior mediastinal mass with heterogeneous enhancement; fat planes with the great vessels and pericardium preserved; no invasion.
Lungs clear; no pleural effusion or pleural nodularity.

body_imaging.impression: 1. Well-circumscribed 3.6 x 2.9 x 3.1 cm anterior mediastinal mass with heterogeneous enhancement and preserved fat planes, most consistent with a thymoma; thymic carcinoma cannot be excluded. 2. No lymphadenopathy, pleural effusion or pleural nodularity. Lungs clear.

interactions: PYRIDOSTIGMINE + METOPROLOL: additive bradycardia (increased vagal tone with beta-blockade). Moderate. Monitor resting heart rate; reduce or hold pyridostigmine for symptomatic bradycardia.

METOPROLOL in myasthenia gravis: beta-blockers can worsen neuromuscular transmission and have been reported to exacerbate MG. Use with caution; consider a non-beta-blocker antihypertensive if weakness worsens.
PREDNISONE + METFORMIN: corticosteroids raise blood glucose and oppose glycaemic control. Moderate. Monitor glucose; diabetes therapy may need escalation.
PYRIDOSTIGMINE or PREDNISONE + LEVOTHYROXINE: no clinically significant interaction.
PREDNISONE + ASPIRIN: increased risk of gastrointestinal bleeding. Moderate. Consider gastroprotection.
pyridostigmine.proposed: pyridostigmine and prednisone; current medications metoprolol succinate 50 mg, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, levothyroxine 75 mcg, aspirin 81 mg
warnings: Metformin and iodinated contrast: no need to withhold metformin when eGFR is above 30 mL/min/1.73m2 and there is no acute kidney injury.

abnormal_values_summary: AChR binding antibody 6.4 nmol/L (H; reference <= 0.02 nmol/L)
labs.interpretation: AChR binding antibody elevated at 6.4 nmol/L, with elevated blocking (55%) and modulating (72%) antibodies. Fasting glucose 128 mg/dL and HbA1c 6.9% elevated. Anti-TPO antibody elevated (148 IU/mL). TSH and free T4 within reference ranges. Blood count and renal function normal. Acetylcholine receptor antibodies are found in most patients with generalized autoimmune myasthenia; clinical correlation recommended.

specialized_test.impression: Abnormal RNS: 3 Hz decrement in deltoid 16%, nasalis 19% and masseter 21% with normal baseline CMAP amplitudes, repair after exercise and post-activation exhaustion; no post-exercise facilitation (6%). Normal nerve conduction studies. Findings are consistent with a postsynaptic disorder of neuromuscular transmission. Clinical correlation recommended.

patient.chief_complaint: Drooping right eyelid and double vision worsening over 6 months
patient.history_present_illness: A 62-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hypothyroidism presented for neurological evaluation of progressive right eyelid drooping and double vision over 6 months. He first noticed intermittent right eyelid drooping approximately 6 months ago, occurring mainly after a full day of work. He is a high school principal and noted the drooping was worst during late-afternoon meetings. Over 3 months, the ptosis became more persistent and began appearing in the morning as well, though it was consistently worse by afternoon. He developed horizontal double vision on looking to the right about 4 months ago. He describes the images as side by side, one in front of the other when looking to the right. He found himself instinctively turning his head to the right to avoid diplopia. Over the past 6 weeks, he has had increasing difficulty chewing steaks and other tough foods — he used to enjoy a steak dinner with his wife on Fridays but has stopped because his jaw gives out after a few bites. He also notices that his voice becomes nasal and harder to understand during long faculty meetings and he has had to shorten his public speaking. He denies sensory symptoms, no limb weakness at rest, no headache, no visual blurring beyond the diplopia. He had a brain MRI performed by his primary care physician that was reported as showing 'mild white matter changes, age-appropriate,' which was reassuring but did not explain his symptoms. His diabetes is well-controlled (HbA1c 6.9%) and he takes levothyroxine for hypothyroidism. He has no family history of neuromuscular disease.

neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Right ptosis, moderate, MRD1 2 mm (left 4 mm). Fatigable ptosis right eye on sustained upgaze at 45 seconds. Diplopia on rightward gaze. Limited right eye abduction. Pupils equal, reactive. Facial weakness bilateral. Voice nasal after prolonged speech.
neurological_exam.gait: Normal casual. Mildly slow on prolonged walking.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented. Normal cognition. Mild fatigue.
neurological_exam.motor: Deltoids 4/5 bilaterally. Hip flexors 4+/5. Neck flexors 4/5. Distal strength 5/5. Fatigability documented.

physical_exam.cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs; no facial or upper limb venous distension.
physical_exam.general: Alert, well-appearing man; right ptosis. Weight 88.1 kg, height 178 cm.
physical_exam.respiratory: Clear to auscultation; no accessory muscle use; SpO2 98% on room air.
